package main

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"sync"

	machine "github.com/whitaker-io/machine/v4"
)

// Order is the payload the embedded-subflow fixture carries.
type Order struct {
	ID   string
	Seen int
	Tags []string
}

// packetCount is how many data the TRANSPORT pushes. It is deliberately ONE
// FEWER than the count the token asserts: main pushes the remaining datum
// in-process through the exported ingest, so the token is reached only if that
// ingest actually delivered into the running graph.
const packetCount = 2

// Feed is the source transport. It pushes a fixed number of packets when the
// machine starts.
func Feed() machine.EdgeFactory[Order] {
	return func(node string, report machine.Report) (machine.Edge[Order], error) {
		return &feedEdge{node: node, ch: make(chan machine.Packet[Order], packetCount)}, nil
	}
}

type feedEdge struct {
	node string
	ch   chan machine.Packet[Order]
	once sync.Once
}

func (e *feedEdge) Start(ctx context.Context) error {
	e.once.Do(func() {
		for i := range packetCount {
			packet, err := machine.RebuildPacket(machine.FrameData{
				ID:     fmt.Sprintf("datum-%d", i),
				Source: e.node,
				Node:   e.node,
			}, Order{ID: fmt.Sprintf("order-%d", i), Tags: []string{"a"}})
			if err != nil {
				return
			}
			e.ch <- packet
		}
	})

	return nil
}

func (e *feedEdge) Send(ctx context.Context, packet machine.Packet[Order]) error {
	select {
	case e.ch <- packet:
		return nil
	case <-ctx.Done():
		return ctx.Err()
	}
}

func (e *feedEdge) Receive() <-chan machine.Packet[Order] { return e.ch }

func (e *feedEdge) Close() error { return nil }

// counted is how many data Count has stamped. It is a plain counter rather than
// a state cell because this fixture's subject is the EMBEDDED SUBFLOW, and a
// state handle would put a second thing under test in the same program.
var (
	countMu sync.Mutex
	counted int
)

// Count stamps each datum with the number seen so far, so the sink's token
// reports how many reached it THROUGH the embedded subflow.
func Count(f machine.Frame[Order]) Order {
	countMu.Lock()
	counted++
	seen := counted
	countMu.Unlock()

	out := f.Value()
	out.Seen = seen

	return out
}

// Interesting is the SUBFLOW's predicate. Everything is interesting, so every
// datum leaves the subflow on its ok output and reaches the sink.
func Interesting(f machine.Frame[Order]) bool { return f.Value().ID != "" }

// done is closed once the token has been printed, so main can exit on the datum
// rather than on a timer.
var done = make(chan struct{})

var emitOnce sync.Once

// Report is the sink. It prints the LOCKED TOKEN from the fixture's own code on
// the third datum, which is reachable only through the embedded subflow.
func Report(f machine.Frame[Order]) Order {
	v := f.Value()
	if v.Seen == packetCount+1 {
		emitOnce.Do(func() {
			fmt.Printf("flow-embed: processed=%d\n", v.Seen)
			close(done)
		})
	}

	return v
}
